scope: Bus. & Prof. Code § 22757.11 as it decides who is bound and what is reportable (foundation model, frontier model, frontier developer, large frontier developer, catastrophic risk, the four kinds of critical safety incident); § 22757.13(a), (c)(1)-(4), (f), (h)-(j) (the 15-day report to the Office of Emergency Services, counted under Code Civ. Proc. §§ 12 and 12a; the 24-hour disclosure; amended and encouraged reports; the report's four items; the Public Records Act exemption; the federal deemed-compliance route); § 22757.15 as it bears on a failure to report (large frontier developers only; up to $1,000,000 per violation; Attorney General only); § 22757.16; SB 53 SEC. 5(d), (e) as inputs. Inert or out of scope, each with a row in NOTES.md: § 22757.12, § 22757.14, § 22757.13(b), (d), (e), (g), the act's SECTION 1, SEC. 3 (CalCompute), SEC. 4 (Labor Code whistleblower sections), SEC. 5(a)-(c), (f), SEC. 6.

forks.F1: Every frontier developer must report (§ 22757.13(c)(1)); only a large one is subject to the § 22757.15 penalty; the chapter states none for others.
forks.F2: Every threshold is strict: more than 10^26 operations, more than $500,000,000, more than 50 people, more than $1,000,000,000.
forks.F3: A frontier model has already used more than 10^26 operations; a frontier developer has trained or begun a foundation model for which it has used or intends to use more than 10^26 (stated as the largest figure over its foundation models).
forks.F4: 'Subject to paragraph (2)': both the 15-day report and the 24-hour disclosure are owed.
forks.F5: A catastrophic risk has 'materialized' when the event it describes, at its stated size, has happened and no exclusion applies.
forks.F6: The four kinds overlap; every kind that fits is listed.
forks.F7: Deployment is not an element of the reporting duty.
forks.F8: § 22757.13(c)(4) read as events that would be critical safety incidents if the model were a frontier model: encouraged, not required.
forks.F9: 15 days: day of discovery excluded, last day included (Code Civ. Proc. § 12); a last day on a Saturday (§ 12a(a)) or a Sunday (§ 135 with Gov. Code § 6700(a)(1)), both computed, or on another § 135 / § 12b holiday the developer lists, moves to the next day that is not a holiday. With no list, the earliest possible last day. Fixed-date and nth-weekday holidays (1 January, Thanksgiving and the day after, and the rest of Gov. Code § 6700 and Code Civ. Proc. § 135) are not computed. Vintage: the deposited § 6700 took effect 2026-03-26; earlier last days rest on that later text.
forks.F10: 'discovering' undefined: the developer states its date of discovery, and the hours since it discovered the imminent risk.
forks.F11: SB 53 SEC. 5(d), (e): inputs; the encoding never decides preemption.
forks.F12: The 24-hour duty is read literally: not limited to the developer's own frontier models.
forks.F13: How violations are counted is not stated; the developer gives a count.
forks.F14: Whether § 22757.15 reaches a failed 24-hour disclosure is not plain; the answer says so.
forks.F15: Incidents discovered before 1 January 2026: not covered.
forks.F16: A disclosure at exactly 24 hours is within 24 hours.
forks.F17: A fine-tuner and the base model's training run (§ 22757.11(i)(2)): not decided; the compute inputs leave it to the developer.
forks.F18: 'the preceding calendar year' (§ 22757.11(j)): preceding the act or the question; not decided, revenue is one input.
forks.F19: 'as required by law' in § 22757.13(c)(2): no recipient is named and nothing is computed from it.
forks.F20: § 22757.13(g): the Office transmits its annual report to the Legislature and the Governor; the text does not say it is published. Inert.
